title: Christening Party Ideas: Food, Decorations and Guest Photos | Albums.ink
desc: Christening party ideas for a baby girl or boy: venue, afternoon tea food, cake, decorations, godparent moments and one QR album for every guest's photos.
h1: Christening party ideas: from the church to the reception, with every guest's photos in one place
lead: Searches for “christening party ideas” in the UK split into the same few questions: where to hold the reception, what food to serve, how to decorate for a baby girl or boy, and how to keep the day simple with a little one in tow. Here are ideas that work for a village hall, a pub function room or your own living room — plus an easy way to collect the photos and videos your guests take.
body: ## Where to hold the christening reception
- At home: the easiest option with a baby — nap times and nappy changes are close at hand.
- A pub function room: many pubs near the church offer a room and a buffet, so nobody has to cook.
- A village or church hall: cheap to hire and big enough for children to run around.
## Food that suits a christening
- Afternoon tea: finger sandwiches, scones with jam and clotted cream, and mini cakes — easy to eat standing up.
- A grazing table or buffet: sausage rolls, quiche, cheese and fruit for all ages.
- The christening cake: a traditional fruit cake or a simple sponge with the baby's name; some families still keep the top tier of their wedding cake for this day.
## Decorations for a baby girl or boy

Soft balloon garlands, white flowers, a welcome sign with the baby's name and the date, and a table with the christening gown or a framed photo from the service. Keep it light — the focus is the baby and the people around them.
## Moments to remember
- Godparents: a photo with each godparent and a short note from them about their promise.
- Four generations: if great-grandparents are there, gather everyone for one photo together.
- Wishes for the baby: a card or jar for messages that the child can read when they are older.
## Collect every guest's photos with one QR code
Grandparents, aunts and godparents will all take photos in the church and at the reception. An event album on Albums gathers them in one place:
1. Create the album, e.g. “Olivia's christening”.
2. Put the QR code on the welcome sign, the tables and the cake table.
3. Guests scan it with their phone camera and upload photos and videos in the browser — nothing to install.
4. Turn on “Hold guest photos” if you want to approve uploads before anyone sees them.
5. Afterwards, download the whole album as one ZIP.
Guests who upload without signing in appear anonymously. Signed-in guests also get a private draft copy of only their own uploads.

Afternoon tea, a buffet with sausage rolls, quiche and fruit, and a christening cake.
Where can I hold a christening reception?
At home, in a pub function room or in a village or church hall near the church.
How do I collect photos from christening guests?
